When to use

Both rows are lists of ways out. The pay list is the content of the pay drawer that the action bar of order-review (and its aerial and inspection variants) opens: three ways to pay is under the picker's count rule, so a list rises instead of a page. The brand buttons come first and DRON's own Pay with card comes last. Pay with card pushes payment, while Apple Pay and Google Pay go straight to payment-loading, because the method is already chosen.

The express buttons are the palette's one licensed exception. HIG · Apple Pay Marks and Buttons and Google Pay's brand guidelines allow a button that starts their payment to be black, white or white with an outline, and nothing else, so they leave the warm ramp on purpose. Their accessible name, Pay with Apple Pay, is on the element; Pay with card is the one option DRON words itself, and it is printed. The card-entry drawer that Add card opens on account-edit is drawn by the card number field and the sheet, not by this list.

The share channels name the place, not the act: Message, Email, More. The verb is the tap.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The pay drawer · inventory.md § 1 (Pay drawer, Card entry drawer) · microcopy.md § order-review, share · voice.md P3

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Pay with card

Express buttons in the brands' black, first; DRON's green Pay with card last, the drawer's only green control.

Don’t

Apple Pay Google Pay Pay with card

Every option green. It breaks both brands' button licence, which a real integration fails at review, and it spends the screen's accent three times: 14.78% of the frame where the rule is ~5%. Express payment wears .dr-btn--pay; only DRON's own option is a primary button.
